lead: A circuit diagram is a graph: nodes are vertices and branches are edges. Network topology studies only this shape, not the element values. A spanning tree is a small connected skeleton with no loop. Every branch outside the tree, called a chord, closes exactly one fundamental tie-set. Every tree branch defines exactly one fundamental cut-set. These sets give the smallest independent set of KVL and KCL equations. Circuit simulators use the same idea to build sparse equations. Only a few universities teach this as a separate topic.
prereq: You need 1.4 for node, branch, loop and mesh, and 1.3 for KVL and KCL.

blocks.text: A graph G = (V, E) has a set V of nodes and a set E of branches. A node is a point where branches meet. A branch is one element or one wire between two nodes. A connected graph has a path between every pair of nodes. In an oriented graph every branch carries an arrow; the arrow fixes the positive current direction and later gives +1 or −1 in a matrix.
Tree branches = n − 1; chords = b − n + 1
blocks.where: n is the number of nodes; b is the number of branches; a chord is a co-tree branch.

blocks.text: A tree is a connected subgraph that contains all n nodes and has no closed path. A tree has exactly n − 1 branches. The co-tree is the rest of the graph. Each co-tree branch is a chord. The number of chords is b − (n − 1) = b − n + 1. The tree is not unique; any valid choice gives the same counts.
In the figure, n = 4 and b = 5. The solid edges A-B, B-C and C-D form one tree. Tree branches = 4 − 1 = 3. Chords = 5 − 4 + 1 = 2; they are D-A and A-C.

A tie-set is a set of branches that forms a closed path, also called a loop. Pick a tree. Remove one chord and keep all tree branches. There is exactly one path in the tree between the two endpoints of the chord. That tree path plus the chord is a fundamental tie-set. Each chord gives one fundamental tie-set, so the count is b − n + 1.

blocks.where: b is the number of branches; n is the number of nodes; each tie-set uses one chord and its unique tree path.

blocks.text: The table shows the two tie-set rows for the figure. Rows are tie-sets and columns are branches. Entry 1 means the branch is in the loop; 0 means it is not. In an oriented graph, use +1 or −1 according to whether the branch arrow agrees with the chosen loop direction.

sections.h3: Cut-sets: one tree branch, one split

blocks.text: A cut-set is a minimal set of branches whose removal splits a connected graph into two separate parts. Minimal means no smaller subset does the job. A fundamental cut-set is made by removing one tree branch. That removal splits the tree, and therefore the graph, into two parts. Collect every branch with one end in each part. The set contains that one tree branch and zero or more chords. Each tree branch gives one fundamental cut-set, so the count is n − 1.

blocks.where: n is the number of nodes; each fundamental cut-set contains exactly one tree branch.

blocks.text: The table shows the three cut-set rows for the figure. A cut-set row gives one KCL equation: the signed sum of branch currents crossing the cut is zero. A tie-set row gives one KVL equation: the signed sum of branch voltages around the loop is zero. The full matrix methods belong to Unit 2, Mesh, Nodal Analysis and Network Theorems.

figure.caption: Solid edges A-B, B-C and C-D form a tree on four nodes. The dashed edge D-A and the edge A-C are chords; each closes one fundamental tie-set with its unique tree path.

spec.aria: A four-node graph with tree branches A-B, B-C and C-D, a dashed chord D-A and a second chord A-C that close two fundamental tie-sets.

examples.question: A connected graph has n = 5 nodes and b = 8 branches. Find the number of tree branches, chords, fundamental tie-sets and fundamental cut-sets. State the rule for one fundamental tie-set.
steps: Chords = b − n + 1 = 8 − 5 + 1 = 4. The value b − n = 3 is wrong because it misses one chord.
Fundamental cut-sets = number of tree branches = 4.
One fundamental tie-set is one chord plus the unique tree path between the two endpoints of that chord.
examples.answer: The graph has 4 tree branches, 4 chords, 4 fundamental tie-sets and 4 fundamental cut-sets.
examples.check:
n = 5
b = 8
tree = n - 1
chords = b - n + 1
tie_sets = chords
cut_sets = tree
print(tree)
print(chords)
print(tie_sets)
print(cut_sets)

traps: Using n instead of n − 1 for the number of tree branches.
Using b − n instead of b − n + 1 for the number of chords. For n = 5 and b = 8, b − n gives 3 but the correct count is 4.
Calling any loop a fundamental tie-set. A fundamental tie-set must be one chord plus its unique tree path.
Calling any group of branches a cut-set. A cut-set must be minimal and must split the graph into two separate parts.
Mixing the counts: fundamental tie-sets equal chords, while fundamental cut-sets equal tree branches, for a connected graph.

quiz.q: In a connected graph with n nodes and b branches, how many branches does a tree have?

quiz.a: A branch of the co-tree, that is, a branch not in the chosen tree.

quiz.q: Why does each chord give exactly one fundamental tie-set?
quiz.a: The chord has two endpoints. The tree has exactly one path between those endpoints. That path plus the chord is one closed loop, so there is one fundamental tie-set for that chord.

quiz.q: Why are there n − 1 fundamental cut-sets in a connected graph with n nodes?
quiz.a: A tree has n − 1 branches. Removing one tree branch splits the tree into two parts and gives one fundamental cut-set. One cut-set per tree branch gives n − 1 cut-sets.

quiz.q: A connected graph has n = 4 nodes and b = 5 branches. Find the number of fundamental tie-sets and fundamental cut-sets.
A connected graph has n = 6 nodes and b = 10 branches. Find tree branches, chords, fundamental tie-sets and fundamental cut-sets.
quiz.a: Tree branches = 6 − 1 = 5. Chords = 10 − 6 + 1 = 5. Fundamental tie-sets = 5. Fundamental cut-sets = 5.

quiz.q: A student says a graph with n = 5 and b = 8 has 3 chords because b − n = 3. Explain the error and give the correct count.
quiz.a: The tree uses n − 1 = 4 branches, not n branches. So chords = b − (n − 1) = b − n + 1 = 8 − 5 + 1 = 4. The student is one short.

quiz.q: A graph has n = 5 and b = 8. A student writes tie-sets = 3 and cut-sets = 5. Identify both errors and give the correct values.
quiz.a: Tie-sets must equal chords = b − n + 1 = 8 − 5 + 1 = 4, not 3. Cut-sets must equal tree branches = n − 1 = 5 − 1 = 4, not 5.

beyond: Not for the exam. Circuit simulators build a spanning tree and use cut-set and tie-set ideas to write sparse KCL and KVL equations. Power-system state estimation uses network topology to detect islanding and bad data. Search "fundamental loop matrix", "fundamental cut-set matrix" and "spanning tree circuit analysis" to go deeper.
